scope: HERMES-COACH-02 C03/C04 local portions and provenance

checks.command: CI=true npm test -- --watchAll=false --runInBand src/services/mealItems.test.js src/services/foodNotes.test.js src/services/mealCommands.test.js src/services/planAllocation.test.js

contracts.catalogMeasureInput: source.measureIndex selects a returned candidate.portions entry; quantity is count in portion; server converts count*grams/amount
contracts.partialLabel: retained ahead of estimate or generic database replacement
contracts.stalePreparedCommand: expectedRevision included in hash; writer persists terminal rejectedSubmissions marker and returns plan_conflict
contracts.quantityTrust: Model proposals need a literal quantity adjacent to this food in actual user text. A canonical single-item draft may bind a reply containing only a quantity. Browser manual edits are explicit user input. Ambiguous, approximate, ranged or negated amounts remain estimates.
contracts.literalBindingLimit: Conservative Ukrainian/Russian/English lexical binding; unrecognized wording keeps estimate provenance and does not block an otherwise valid food entry.
contracts.completeLabel: Concrete label remains ahead of a same-food model estimate. A genuinely named new product or an attached new label may replace it.
contracts.completeSourceKeys: JS complete-item and note validators reject keys outside the source contract. New portion origin validates kind and a nonempty assumption of at most 400 characters.
contracts.legacyImportProof: Existing confirmLegacy writer adds legacyImportProfileId in the same transaction as copying historical rows and clearing legacyMeals; proof validation belongs to the separate rules verification.
contracts.newLabelQuantity: Current explicit quantity for the named food, or a canonical single-item quantity-only reply, wins over the prior consumed quantity. Otherwise a photo changes nutrients while retaining the old portion.
contracts.retainedConcreteStatus: After retaining concrete nutrition and changing quantity, recompute itemProblems before choosing complete versus unknown.

acceptedCases: different food weight cannot imply a precise portion
negated, alternative, range, approximate, upper-bound and questioned masses stay estimates
literal named food weight is precise
bare quantity reply requires exactly one canonical existing draft item
complete and partial concrete labels outrank a same-food model estimate
unknown source keys fail complete-item validation

findings: Retained label after quantity clarification recomputes nutritionStatus in both directions.
A new photographed label accepts a current literal quantity bound to the same item; absent or ambiguous new quantity preserves prior consumed portion.
Common gram abbreviations гр and гр. match exact user quantities without accepting approximate or different-food weights.

rulesFollowup.scope: complete-item strict source delta guard, legacy import proof, expression budget and adversarial cases; no current rules success claimed here
